newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spot Prods--Gulf gasoline diffs enjoy bounce.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spot Prods--Gulf gasoline diffs enjoy bounce.

text.p: Prompt U.S. Gulf conventional gasoline differentials popped higher by late Thursday as traders chased prices up ahead of a scheduling deadline on the Colonial Pipeline.
On the NYMEX, July gasoline fell 0.18 cent and August gasoline fell 0.45 cent. July heating oil futures fell 0.97 cent and August heating oil dropped 0.95 cent.
U.S. GULF COAST

Prompt regular coventional M1 gasoline jumped to as high as 1.60 cents under August futures near midday, a gain of more than 1.00 cent. But it slipped back below 2.00 cents under late in the day -- still about a half cent over Wednesday diffs.

Market players said the scheduling deadline at the end of the day on the Colonial Pipeline, the main artery from the Gulf to the East Coast, forced players to cover commitments and helped drive prices up.
"This happens on scheduling deadlines about seven times out of ten," one trader said. "It just seems to be a dice roll on whether everyone gets covered by noon" causing prices to fall back, he added.

The strength in prompt coventionals helped boost early August M1 gasolines as well, traders said. Early August M1 jumped to about 2.00 cents under the August NYMEX, though the differential had slipped back to about 2.50 to 2.75 cents under the NYMEX by the end of the day.
Prompt premium conventional V1 gasoline slipped slightly Thursday to between 4.75 to 5.00 cents over the regular M1 gasoline, according to players.
NEW YORK HARBOR
Activity in the Harbor was extremely subdued Thursday, traders said, with few players making deals despite the very ample supplies.
Regular conventional M2 gasoline continued to hover near 3.00 cents under the July futures, though no particular feature to the market was noted.

However, the arbitrage window with Europe appeared nearly ready to reopen after being closed for some time. An increase in New York gasoline prices of about 0.50 cent a gallon or decrease in European priced of the same level would restart the market, one trader said.
Prompt reformulated A2 gasoline sat unchanged on the day at about 0.50 cent under the July NYMEX.
MIDCONTINENT
Group Three differentials on prompt low sulfur diesel slumped over a half cent by mid-afternoon, with parcels sold for 1.60 cents over July futures amid more-than-ample supply, traders said.
"There's plenty of diesel available for agricultural demand," one trader said, noting diffs had widened earlier in the week as supplies were stocked for harvests in the region.
"But it got overbought and is now coming back to normal," the trader said.

In the Chicago market, prompt products began being quoted against the August NYMEX screen. Prompt diesel for early July delivery was sold for 0.35 cent below the August print, about 0.35 cent weaker than Wednesday diffs.

Gasoline diffs were little changed, with Group Three conventional unleaded sold for 4.50 cents above July futures and Chicago material offered at about 0.90 cents over the August screen, traders said.
